newsitem.title: USA: Northwest Wash. gas lines back in a few days.
newsitem.headline: Northwest Wash. gas lines back in a few days.

text.p: Northwest Pipeline Corp, a unit of the Williams Cos, said Monday it expected repairs to two damaged natural gas lines in Washington to be completed "in the next few days".
The company had two line ruptures over the weekend on its 26-inch diameter pipeline, one on February 8 near Everson, Washington, and a second on February 9 near Kalama, Wash.
"The cause of both ruptures is still unknown and under investigation. The two incidents are not related," the company said in a statement.
Northwest switched service to a parallel, 30-inch diamter line, avoiding service interruptions to local gas customers.
The company said it is working with the U.S. Department of Transportation Office of Pipeline Safety and state agencies to investigate the causes of the ruptures.

Northwest, headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah, operates a 4,000-mile high pressure natural gas transmission system that originates in the San Juan Basin in northwestern New Mexico and extends to the U.S.-Canadian border at Sumas, Washington.
